Silence on joue ! est le podcast jeu vid: Silence on joue ! is the video game podcast of Libération, launched in 2007 — nineteen years, more than 940 episodes. Back then, the iPhone had just come out and nobody talked about "content creators" yet. While empires rose and fell, they published every week. It's by far the oldest French video game podcast still running: not a trendy show, a monument.
Ce qui tient dix-neuf ans, ce n'est pas: What lasts nineteen years isn't a concept, it's a gang. Erwan Cario hosts — a former developer turned journalist, he has the most thankless role: passing the mic around, reframing, relaunching. Around him, Marius Chapuis, Patrick Hellio, Julie Le Baron and Corentin Benoit-Gonin. And a special case, Jérémie Kletzkine, whose board game segment has become a podcast in its own right.
Donnez le jeu de l'année à Marius Chapui: Give Marius Chapuis the game of the year and he'll find what's wrong with it. It isn't bad temper, it's disappointed high standards: his praise is rare, so it's worth something.
Patrick Hellio replace un jeu dans sa li: Patrick Hellio places a game in its lineage and reminds you that the announced revolution already existed in 1998. Without him you comment on the news; with him you do criticism.
La chronique jeu de société de Jérémie K: Jérémie Kletzkine's board game segment worked so well that it's re-released as a standalone podcast a week after the episode. That says something about the house: they let people exist.
Le format n'a quasiment pas bougé depuis: The format has barely changed since 2007: the week's games, in depth, everyone gives their opinion, they debate and contradict each other. No rebranding, no vertical version, no "new formula". And that's precisely why we trust them. The divisive point — an openly left-wing editorial line — is in our view a strength: a stated point of view is more honest than feigned neutrality. Video game criticism spent twenty years pretending to rate only technique and play time, as if a game were just a product. Here they look at who made it, under what conditions, and what it says about work and power.
Trois réserves, toutes concédées de bonn: Three reservations, all conceded with good grace. The openly stated line mechanically limits the audience: a strong tone strongly unites and strongly excludes, you can't have both. Sometimes the social analysis takes over from the game — you came to find out if it's good and leave with twenty minutes of social debate and still no answer. Finally, the weekly format depends on the news: if the week is weak, so is the episode, however good the gang. A podcast about older works, like Fin du Game, doesn't have that problem. And the half: nineteen years of complicity produce codes and inside jokes — delightful when you're in, a wall when you arrive.
Par où commencer : surtout pas au hasard: Where to start: definitely not at random. Look for the episode about a game you've finished — that's where the value shows, because you'll be able to argue with them. And stay for the board game segment: often the best fifteen minutes, even if you've never touched a board.
« Ce ne sera jamais le podcast jeu vidéo: “It will never be France's most listened-to video game podcast, because they chose having taste over maximising listeners. It's a choice I deeply respect.”
